questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Malta?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Malta article.

questions.proof: The capital of Malta is Valletta.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Malta?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Language” part of the Malta article.

questions.proof: Maltese is the national language of Malta.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “They moved to Malta after being forced to leave _____ and then Rhodes, in Greece.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “leave”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Malta article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: They moved to Malta after being forced to leave Palestine and then Rhodes, in Greece.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Malta became independent in _____ and a republic in 1974.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Malta article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: Malta became independent in 1964 and a republic in 1974.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The French rule was not popular and in _____ Maltese rebels invited the British Royal Navy to come to the island.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the eighteenth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Malta article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: The French rule was not popular and in 1800 Maltese rebels invited the British Royal Navy to come to the island.
